bifrost: none for app-facing accessory sessions; OS layer: springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs (device list, pairing, audio route flag), springboard/src/shell/pages.rs (bluetooth_spec, line 378), springboard/src/bare/input.rs (evdev input devices, shell only), springboard/src/media/v4l2.rs (camera devices, shell only)
summary: Apple's framework connects apps to MFi hardware over Lightning, 30-pin or Bluetooth with a per-protocol byte stream. BifrOSt gives USB accessories the same shape: the shell reads the bus, the person grants one device per app, and the app gets connect and disconnect notifications, an accessory object, a session on usb.vvvv.pppp and a transport that moves the session's streams over bulk or interrupt endpoints (bifrost_app::external_accessory, usb_access). Bluetooth MFi, Lightning, MFi authentication and Wi-Fi accessory setup have no counterpart.

features.bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/external_accessory.rs (AccessoryManager, register_for_notifications, take_events); springboard/core/src/accessory_manager.rs (AccessoryManager::sync); tests: springboard/sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs, springboard/src/shell/services/usb_access.rs, springboard/sdk/src/usb_access.rs
features.note: Apps register for connect and disconnect notifications and take them in order, and a registration that is cancelled drops the queue; tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: no bus source drives attach and detach on a real device, which needs hardware and a Midget check. Refreshed 2026-10-17: the manager, registration and the notification queue are covered by sdk external_accessory.rs (AccessoryManager, register_for_notifications, take_events; tests external_accessory::tests). Only the bus source that drives attach and detach on a device remains. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): The bus source now runs: the shell's usb service polls /sys/bus/usb/devices once a second into the accessory manager, and sends each app connect and disconnect events for the devices it was granted. AccessoryManager::apply_usb_event and sync_usb_devices turn those into attach and detach with the notification queue. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (external_accessory::tests::usb_events_attach_and_detach_and_notify_a_registered_app) and cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::a_plug_of_a_granted_device_is_announced_to_that_app_only; on the device: grant a USB device, unplug and replug it and watch the events.

features.note: Accessory::from_core builds the app view (identity, protocol strings, connection id, connected state) from the USB accessory manager record, tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: wired accessories are not modelled, and no bus event feeds the view yet, which needs hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): accessory_from_usb builds the app view from a granted device: name, serial from the device id, one protocol string, and a connection id that stays the same across a replug of the same serial number. Wired non-USB accessories are not modelled. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (external_accessory::tests::a_granted_usb_device_becomes_an_accessory_with_one_protocol_and_a_stable_id).

Protocol strings match exactly, a session is refused for a disconnected accessory or an undeclared protocol, and the matches are listed in attach order; tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: no manifest key declares accessory protocols and the sandbox grants no accessory device, so an app cannot reach hardware yet. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): A USB accessory declares one protocol, usb.vvvv.pppp (external_accessory::usb_protocol), so session(accessory, protocol) works with the same call. A manifest key for declared protocols is not built; the usb permission and the person's sheet are the gate. Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer::; usb_events_attach_and_detach_and_notify_a_registered_app opens a session on the protocol.

features.note: A session carries bytes in both directions through its input and output streams, and closing refuses writes; tested headless in sdk/tests/parity_sdk-complete-14.rs. Gap: the transport that moves bytes to and from a real accessory needs hardware. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): UsbTransport moves a session's bytes: a bulk or interrupt IN endpoint feeds the input stream and the output stream goes out the OUT endpoint in chunks, one read and one write in flight, read timeouts retried, other failures reported by error(). Midget check: cargo test -p bifrost-app usb_access:: external_accessory:: usb_printer:: (external_accessory::tests::the_transport_reads_continuously_and_sends_output_in_chunks); on the device with a loopback or serial device: open, claim, run UsbTransport, write to the session's output stream and read the echo.

features.note: Audit 2026-10-13: the row predated this code. Pure model with host unit tests (serial_ports.rs, serial_ports.rs, external_accessory.rs, usb_descriptors.rs); not wired into the shell or apps, not tested on Midget. Checked for serial and USB device access in springboard/ with a text search: only the PTY (springboard/src/term/pty.rs), the installer and the DRM driver (springboard/wm/src/drm.rs) matched. Recorded for completeness; the USB side belongs to the AccessoryAccess matrix row. 2026-10-19 (wave 15, usb): USB accessories are reachable end to end through the usb service (consent sheet, claim, bulk and control I/O); serial-class devices (CDC, FTDI vendor-specific) work when their interface is not a protected class. serial_ports.rs (PTY serial lines) is unchanged. Midget check: cargo test -p springboard --features desktop-wayland usb_access::; on the device: plug a USB serial adapter (vendor-specific interface) into Midget, run an app that declares `usb` in its manifest and calls usb_access::request from the front window.

gaps: The app view of an accessory (Accessory::from_core) has no bus source yet, and the sandbox binds no accessory device nodes.

No manifest key or sandbox grant for accessory protocols (app_policy.rs binds only /dev/snd and /dev/dri), so an app cannot reach a declared accessory. The EASession byte streams exist as a model (sdk external_accessory Session)

The Bluetooth picker request model exists (sdk bluetooth_picker, tests bluetooth_picker::tests), but the request does not cross the shell boundary, so no app can open it; the pairing sheet stays in the shell
No Wi-Fi unconfigured accessory browser or configuration flow.

The SDK has a Bluetooth device model (sdk bluetooth_devices: RemoteDevice, DeviceList, tests bluetooth_devices::tests), but the shell keeps its own table in springboard/src/bare/bluetooth.rs and no app can reach the list
